subject: SLO measurement, monitoring evidence and acceptance playbook
messages:
From: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acmecorp.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO measurement and monitoring questionnaire

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking this procurement packet. Our security and SRE team have a few follow-ups specific to availability and latency measurement before we finalize the vendor evaluation. Can you please provide: 

- A concise description of how Redwood defines "uptime" and "availability" for hosted inference endpoints (measurement windows, regional aggregation).
- The exact Prometheus/Grafana queries (or equivalent) used to compute p95/p99 latency and availability; sample output or CSV for Q1 2025 is ideal.
- Monitoring retention and how long raw telemetry (token-level traces, error logs) is retained for audit/forensic purposes.
- Your alerting thresholds and escalation flow for sustained latency degradation (e.g., p99 > X ms for Y mins).
- Whether we get read-only dashboard access (Grafana) and if you can provide a temporary readonly API token for our integration testing.
- Any documented exception process for SLOs during planned maintenance or region failover (how customers are notified and how credits/SLAs are handled).

We'd like to have the evidence packet and a signed playbook by next Wednesday (6/4) if possible. If some items require an NDA addendum (e.g., raw trace samples) let us know.

Best,
Jenna Ortiz
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp

From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acmecorp.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO measurement and monitoring questionnaire

Hi Jenna — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together an evidence packet and short playbook; attaching the CSV extract and a sample incident-replay file. Key answers below and a few links: 

- Availability definition: uptime = percentage of successful 2xx/206 responses from the public inference endpoint evaluated across regional probes. We compute availability per-region and globally over 1m rolling windows with a 7d and 30d SLA roll-up for reporting.
- Latency: p95 and p99 are measured on the server-side request completion time (end-to-end processing time excluding client network) using our ingestion of request start/end events. Typical queries: "sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)" and a p99 calculation using histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)). I'll include exported Grafana panels in the drive link.
- Retention: aggregated metrics (Prometheus-style histograms/counters) retained for 13 months. Raw token-level traces and full request payloads are retained for 90 days by default; can be extended under contract up to 12 months with an add-on.
- Alerting & escalation: default customer alerting policy: p99 latency > 1200ms for 10 continuous minutes triggers P1 pager and auto-creates incident in our ops board; p99 > 500ms for 30 minutes triggers P2 and email escalation to account CS. We can provide customer-facing threshold suggestions; thresholds are adjustable per-customer via the Dedicated offering.
- Dashboard access: we can provide a temporary read-only Grafana invite and a short-lived API token for scripted queries. I've attached the invite stub (grafana_readonly_invite.txt).
- Exception path: planned maintenance windows are scheduled (48h notice) and are excluded from SLA if announced through the console and email. Unplanned regional failovers have a documented exception policy: if failover causes >1% additional downtime, customers are eligible for credits per the contract. We capture failover events and produce incident replays on request.

Attachments included: uptime_report_2025-Q1.csv (sample), incident-replay-sample.json, grafana_readonly_invite.txt. Drive playbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-playbook-link

If any of the attached artifacts contain sensitive traces you need redacted, we can produce a redacted export under NDA. Let me know which exact Grafana panels your SREs want and I'll provision access.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@acmecorp.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jun 2025 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO measurement and monitoring questionnaire

Thanks Aisha — packet looks good. A couple quick clarifications from our SRE review: 

1) For the p99 calculation you mentioned histogram_quantile on 5m buckets — can you also share a sample of the raw bucket counts (not just the histogram panel) for a transit window where an incident occurred? We want to verify the bucket boundaries you use.

2) Incident replays: can you provide one example replay where a regional spike caused retries and explain how prefix caching affected observed latency for subsequent requests?

3) For retention: we need at least 6 months of raw traces for our compliance audit. Is an extension to 180 days available as a procurement add-on and what is the cost ballpark?

If you can reply with the raw bucket sample and a short note on replay mechanics, we can sign the playbook and proceed to PO.

- Jenna

Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO measurement and monitoring questionnaire

Hi Jenna — looping in a quick follow-up from the product side. We attached the raw bucket sample and an annotated incident replay that shows the prefix-caching effect you asked about (attached as incident-replay-sample.json). Two quick notes: 

- Bucket sample: see the attached CSV (uptime_report_2025-Q1.csv) with a second tab showing the histogram bucket counts during the March regional spike; bucket boundaries are 50ms/100ms/250ms/500ms/1s/2s/5s. That sample is what we use to derive histogram_quantile.

- Replay & prefix cache: the incident replay includes traces that show an initial latency spike due to backend autoscaling delays. Subsequent requests benefit from warm KV cache (prefix caching) which reduces tail latency but can obscure cold-start effects in a short sample window; we annotate the replay to highlight where caching changes the distribution so you can reproduce it in your tests.

On retention: we can extend raw trace retention to 180 days as an add-on. I'll have procurement share a ballpark price in the PO addendum — expect a 20–35% uplift on the telemetry add-on, depending on region and encryption options.

Next steps I propose:
- We provision a read-only Grafana link and temporary API token (we've already staged the invite; see grafana_readonly_invite.txt).
- We send a one-page signed acceptance playbook (attached in the drive link) and a DocuSign PO template.

If that works, we can sign the playbook and move to PO on Thursday.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
